_note.why: Who is shooting at you, and how tough they are. This file exists so those numbers live in versioned data rather than in the GM model's response. The model used to write every hostile's REF, BODY, HP, SP, attack skill and damage dice inside prompt guidance ('Mooks are ordinary people: REF 5-7, BODY 5-6, HP 25-35...'), which meant the narrator set how hard each fight was, in the moment, knowing how the scene was going.
_note.provenance: These are house profiles, NOT verbatim book statblocks — do not cite a page for them. They are calibrated against the one published NPC ladder already transcribed in this repo: the Lawman's Backup tiers (roles.json, roles.lawman.roleAbility.mechanics.tiers), which run from Corporate Security at Combat 8 / SP 7 / HP 20 up to C-SWAT at Combat 15 / SP 18 / HP 35. Where a profile names one of those groups, its numbers match that table.
_note.combatNumber: The Backup table prints a single combined Combat Number that a d10 is added to. A hostile here splits it into ref + attackSkill because that is how engine/combat.ts builds an attack (STAT + Skill + 1d10). ref + attackSkill equals the Combat Number the ladder prints, so the arithmetic lands in the same place.
_note.rangeType: Must be one of the printed range types in engine/combatTables.ts. The engine reads the Range DV off that table and the measured distance; nothing here sets a DV.
_note.move: MOVE in metres per Move Action, matching the Backup table's move column. The engine bounds how far a hostile can walk with it.
_note.forceBudget: Force sizes are budgeted for ONE Edgerunner, because that is who plays this game. Cyberpunk RED: Single Player Mode gives the encounter guideline as roughly one Mook per PC for a challenging but generally winnable fight, one Lieutenant per two PCs, and one Mini-Boss per three. A solo protagonist therefore tops out at one Mook before a fight stops being fair. These sizes used to be built for a crew — 'small' was two Mooks and 'standard' was four — which is where the action economy that killed the character in playtesting came from: four hostile Actions for every one of theirs, before a single Morale check could ever fire. The old sets are kept as 'overwhelming', which is not an encounter. It is a problem to be solved another way.
_note.forceGoal: Why they are fighting, per Cyberpunk RED: Single Player Mode, which tells the solo player to establish the opposition's reason before the shooting. Every fight in this app used to have the same implicit answer — reduce the player to zero and keep going — which for a character with no Medtech and no crew is how a campaign ends rather than how a fight goes. A force with a goal stops when the goal is met. The engine reads only 'is there still a reason to shoot'; what they take with them is the narrator's.

profiles.name: Street Thug
profiles.note: Somebody's muscle, in a jacket that has been shot before. Combat 8, the bottom of the ladder.

profiles.name: Scavver
profiles.note: In it for the parts. Hits hard up close and cannot reach past a room.

profiles.name: Ganger
profiles.note: Colours, a cheap SMG, and something to prove. Combat 10, level with a beat cop.

profiles.name: Boostergang Chromer
profiles.note: Chromed past reason. Faster on their feet than anything else at this tier, and armoured for it.

profiles.name: Corporate Security
profiles.note: Renta-cops on foot with Heavy Pistols and Kevlar. Straight off the published Backup ladder: Combat 8, SP 7, HP 20, MOVE 4.

profiles.name: Beat Cop
profiles.note: NCPD on the street. Published ladder: Combat 10, SP 7, HP 25, MOVE 5.

profiles.name: Enforcer
profiles.note: The one giving orders. A rifle changes the shape of a fight: it is the only tier here that shoots comfortably across a street.

profiles.name: Militech Contractor
profiles.note: Expensive, professional, on a schedule. Calibrated to the Sheriff's Department rung: Combat 14, SP 13, HP 35.

profiles.name: Solo
profiles.note: Somebody who does this for a living. Fast, armoured, and the reason the job went wrong.

profiles.name: Overwatch
profiles.note: Wants to be 100m away and will walk backwards to stay there — the printed sniper table is worst up close, which the engine reads without being told.

_note.source: Cyberpunk RED: Single Player Mode (R. Talsorian Games, 2025) — encounter composition guidance.
_note.why: The guideline is given per PC: about one Mook each for a challenging but winnable fight, one Lieutenant per two, one Mini-Boss per three. This expresses the same ratio as a MOOK-EQUIVALENT cost so a mixed force can be weighed in one number.
_note.derivation: A Lieutenant budgeted at one per two PCs costs what two Mooks cost. A Mini-Boss at one per three costs three. This repo has no Mini-Boss tier, so its bosses take the 3 slot. The arithmetic is ours; the ratios it encodes are the book’s.
_note.use: Never to refuse a fight. Cyberpunk is allowed to put six Tyger Claws in front of one person — the point is that the game should KNOW that is not a fair fight, and say so, rather than presenting it as an encounter to be won by standing still and shooting.
